title: Slave Trade and Urban Slavery on the Swahili Coast from Medieval Times to Abolition
locator: Abstract and medieval c.750-1500 synthesis; steady but not massive export; dependence complexity
claim_fitness: Strong for persistent medieval slave-trade participation and for constraining scale/uniformity; not port-by-port exact-1400 evidence

title: When Did the Swahili Become Maritime?
locator: Discussion of Rasulid Yemen customs, late-14th-century Qadi Masud, regular voyages and eastern African commodities including slaves
claim_fitness: Strong for regular thirteenth/fourteenth-century East Africa-Arabia maritime structure with slaves among traded commodities; unfit to prove every Swahili node or cargo carried slaves

dependency_note: Specific customs claims depend partly on Rasulid/Yemeni source scholarship including Vallet; preserve that dependency

title: Ibn Battuta on slaves at Kilwa

claim_fitness: Strong for enslaved presence/transfer at Kilwa and for reported ruler raiding; does not establish coast-wide prevalence or slave-export volume
access_limitation: Modern English translation/reproduction read; Arabic text not independently edited in this pass
dependency_note: Teaching page and Freeman-Grenville translation are one Ibn Battuta textual chain, not independent witnesses

title: No such thing as invisible people: toward an archaeology of slavery at the fifteenth-century Swahili site of Songo Mnara

claim_fitness: Strong bounded specialist interpretation for likely enslaved workers at Songo Mnara; material proxies are ambiguous and do not quantify or generalize prevalence
access_limitation: Open-access full text read; proxy-status ambiguity explicitly preserved
dependency_note: Already represented in repository site case; reuse is dependency-aware and not counted as a new independent discovery

title: Traces of Clay: Exploring Slave and Migrant Identities in Medieval Swahili Zanzibar
locator: Tumbatu/Mkokotoni c.1000-1400; outlier pottery; medieval slavery/migration discussion; explicit scale and status limits
claim_fitness: Useful for c.1400 archaeological context and for distinguishing enslaved people from migrants/dependents; does not prove slave status of individual potters or quantify scale
access_limitation: Open-access Cambridge article read; broad historical discussion partly depends on Vernet and Rødland et al. 2020
dependency_note: Separate site dataset but interpretive background overlaps earlier Swahili slavery scholarship; do not double-count broad claims
